questions.ask: What exactly does a TE node denote? Please give a gloss, example, and its principal relations.
Does a termination point specifically denote a node-owned edge point terminating a TE link, or a broader kind of endpoint? Please give a gloss, example, and relations.
What does a supporting TP represent, especially how it models inter-layer adaptation? Please give a gloss, example, and relations.
What does a tunnel termination point denote, and how does it differ from an ordinary termination point or tunnel connection endpoint? Please give a gloss, example, and relations.
Does a TE tunnel denote an externally requested end-to-end connectivity service, an internal realization of one, or something else? Please give a gloss, example, and relations.
What information does an OTN label express? In particular, does it encode multiplexing/layer structure such as ODU2 mapped into OTU4? Please give a gloss, example, and relations.
Does a connectivity matrix express constraints on permitted cross-connects among ports within a node? Please give a gloss, example, and relations.
What precisely is a TE link, including its endpoints and containment relations? Please give a gloss, example, and relations.
What precisely is a TE topology, and can it be a single multi-layer domain topology? Please give a gloss, example, and relations.
What does a tunnel connection endpoint denote, and how is it related to a tunnel and a node? Please give a gloss, example, and relations.

answers.gloss: A traffic-engineering node representing a node within one particular layer network.
answers.example: ROADM R1 represented in the OTN layer.
answers.relations: It is part of i.tetopo; i.tp, i.ttp, i.cmatrix, and i.tcep may be located on it, while i.telink connects it to other TE nodes.

answers.gloss: A node-owned edge termination point at which a TE link terminates; it is not a generic service or tunnel endpoint.
answers.example: The termination point on R1 facing the R1–R2 TE link.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and terminates i.telink. Through i.stp, it may be supported by a termination point in a server layer.

answers.gloss: The supporting-termination relationship by which a client-layer TP is supported by a server-layer TP, thereby representing inter-layer adaptation.
answers.example: An OTN termination point at R1 supported by an optical-layer termination point at R1.
answers.relations: It links supporting and supported instances of i.tp across layers; unlike i.tp, it denotes the adaptation/support relationship rather than an ordinary link endpoint.

answers.gloss: The trail-head point at which an end-to-end TE tunnel originates or terminates.
answers.example: The A1 trail head of the A1–A3 ODU2 tunnel.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and originates or terminates i.tunnel. It differs from i.tp, which terminates a TE link, and from i.tcep, which is an endpoint of an internal tunnel connection at a node.

answers.gloss: An end-to-end traffic-engineered tunnel that realizes connectivity for a service across a TE topology.
answers.example: The A1–A3 ODU2 tunnel.
answers.relations: It begins and ends at instances of i.ttp, traverses i.tetopo, contains or is realized through i.tcep endpoints, and may be assigned i.otnlabel multiplexing information.

answers.gloss: An OTN forwarding or multiplexing label expressing tributary-slot and tributary-port-number structure, including how a lower-rate ODU is multiplexed into a higher-rate container.
answers.example: The TS/TPN selection carrying an ODU2 inside an OTU4.
answers.relations: It labels i.tunnel with OTN multiplexing information; it is not itself the tunnel or topology.

answers.gloss: A node-local matrix specifying which internal connectivity or cross-connect combinations are permitted.
answers.example: The connectivity matrix defining allowed cross-connects within R2.
answers.relations: It is associated with i.tenode and constrains internal switching among that node's relevant termination or connection points.

answers.gloss: A traffic-engineering link connecting TE nodes within one layer network.
answers.example: The R1–R2 TE link.
answers.relations: It lies within i.tetopo, runs between instances of i.tenode, and is terminated at its ends by instances of i.tp.

answers.gloss: A traffic-engineering network for a particular layer, containing that layer's TE nodes and TE links; in this model it is per-layer rather than one undifferentiated multi-layer topology.
answers.example: The OTN layer network.
answers.relations: It contains i.tenode and i.telink and provides the topology over which i.tunnel is routed. Separate layer topologies may be related through supporting TPs.

answers.gloss: An endpoint of a tunnel connection within a node, associated with the tunnel's internal realization.
answers.example: The connection endpoint for the A1–A3 tunnel on R1.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and is part of i.tunnel. Unlike i.ttp, it is an internal connection endpoint and not specifically the end-to-end trail head; unlike i.tp, it does not terminate a TE link.

questions.ask: Does this denote a node in a particular layer topology, or a physical/multi-layer aggregate node? Please give its gloss, an example, and principal relations.
Does this specifically terminate a topology link on a node, and can it also participate in inter-layer support? Please give its gloss, example, and relations.
Does a transitional link denote an inter-layer adaptation relationship between termination points, or a link-like resource with distinct endpoints? Please give its gloss, example, and relations.
What boundary or access function does a service-interface point represent, and how does it relate to services, nodes, and termination points? Please give a gloss, example, and relations.
Does a connectivity service denote an externally requested service, an engineered tunnel realizing one, or both? Please give its gloss, example, and relations.

What information does a layer-protocol qualifier encode, particularly whether it identifies multiplexing structure such as ODU2 in OTU4 or tributary slots? Please give a gloss, example, and relations.
What does a node-rule group constrain or permit within a node, and is it equivalent to a matrix of allowed internal cross-connects? Please give a gloss, example, and relations.
What kind of link does this denote, what are its endpoints, and in what topology is it contained? Please give a gloss, example, and relations.
Is this topology per layer or potentially a multi-layer/domain aggregate, and what does it contain? Please give a gloss, example, and relations.
What kind of connection endpoint does this denote, and how is it related to a service, connection, node, SIP, or LTP? Please give a gloss, example, and relations.

answers.gloss: A forwarding node represented in the single multi-layer domain topology, rather than a separate node object restricted to one layer.
answers.example: ROADM R1 in the OTN-over-optical topology.
answers.relations: It is part of t.topo; t.ltp, t.sip, t.nrg, and t.cep are located on it, t.link connects nodes, and t.translink expresses adaptation at it.

answers.gloss: A node-owned edge point at which a topological link terminates.
answers.example: The R1 edge point facing the R1-R2 link.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and terminates t.link. Inter-layer adaptation is represented separately by t.translink rather than by an explicit supporting-TP relation on t.ltp.

answers.gloss: A link-like adaptation construct expressing transition between layers at a node.
answers.example: The OTU4-to-ODU2 adaptation at R1.
answers.relations: It is at t.node and adapts the layer or multiplexing structure represented by t.lpq. It is distinct from the ordinary node-to-node topology link t.link; the model does not define it merely as a relationship between two t.ltp instances.

answers.gloss: A network-boundary access point through which an external client service accesses the network.
answers.example: The ODU2 client hand-off at A1.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and provides access to t.cs. It is an external service interface, not a topology-link termination point or an internal connection endpoint.

answers.gloss: An externally meaningful end-to-end connectivity service across the network, not merely an engineered tunnel that realizes another service.
answers.example: The A1-A3 ODU2 connectivity service.
answers.relations: It uses t.sip access points, is realized internally by t.cep endpoints, and runs over t.topo.

answers.gloss: A qualifier describing a signal's layer and multiplexing structure.
answers.example: ODU2 mapped into an OTU4 server.
answers.relations: It qualifies t.cs and is the structure adapted by t.translink. It captures the multiplexing/layer arrangement, but the model does not specifically define it as a forwarding label or require explicit tributary-slot and tributary-port-number fields.

answers.gloss: A node-local rule group constraining which ports or points may be cross-connected.
answers.example: The set of permitted cross-connects within R2.
answers.relations: It is associated with t.node and governs allowed internal switching combinations.

answers.gloss: A topological link between two forwarding nodes in the single multi-layer topology.
answers.example: The R1-R2 link.
answers.relations: It is contained in t.topo, lies between t.node instances, and is terminated by t.ltp instances.

answers.gloss: The single multi-layer topology describing the entire network domain.
answers.example: The combined OTN-over-optical domain topology.
answers.relations: It contains t.node and t.link and carries t.cs. Unlike a strictly per-layer topology model, its nodes and links coexist in one multi-layer topology.

answers.gloss: An endpoint of an internal connection realizing a connectivity service within a node.
answers.example: The endpoint for the A1-A3 service on R1.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and part of the realization of t.cs. It is neither the external access point t.sip nor the edge point t.ltp that terminates a topology link.

proposals.rationale: Both denote forwarding or TE nodes that own points and are connected by links. The representational scope differs: t.node belongs to one multi-layer topology, whereas i.tenode represents a node in a particular layer network.
Both specifically denote node-owned edge points terminating topological or TE links.

Both represent inter-layer adaptation or support. The difference is structural: t.translink is modeled as an adaptation link at a node, while i.stp is explicitly a support relationship between client- and server-layer termination points.

Both express OTN layer and multiplexing structure such as ODU2 carried in OTU4. i.otnlabel is a concrete forwarding/multiplexing label with TS/TPN details, while t.lpq is a more abstract layer-protocol qualifier.
Both are node-local constructs specifying or constraining permitted internal cross-connect combinations.
Both connect nodes and terminate at node-owned termination points. t.link exists in a unified multi-layer topology, while i.telink is scoped to one layer network.

Both are topology containers for nodes and links and provide the domain over which connectivity is carried. Their granularity materially differs: t.topo is one multi-layer domain topology, whereas i.tetopo is a separate per-layer TE topology.

Both denote node-local endpoints of an internal end-to-end connectivity realization and are not link termination points. Their parent constructs differ because t.cep realizes t.cs, while i.tcep belongs to i.tunnel.
Both denote a node-owned edge termination point at which a topology or TE link terminates.
Both denote a node-local specification of permitted internal cross-connect or switching combinations.
Both denote a node-local endpoint of an internal connection used to realize end-to-end connectivity, distinct from an external access point and a topology-link termination point.

ratifications.reason: i.tenode is explicitly a node representation within one particular layer network, whereas t.node is a single aggregate forwarding-node representation in a multi-layer topology. They have related roles but do not denote the same modeled entity.
Both specifically denote node-owned edge points terminating topology or TE links.

i.stp denotes an explicit support relationship between client- and server-layer termination points. t.translink is instead a link-like adaptation construct at a node and is expressly not defined merely as that TP-to-TP support relationship.

i.otnlabel is a concrete OTN forwarding or multiplexing label expressing tributary-slot and TPN selection. t.lpq is a broader abstract qualifier of layer and multiplexing structure and need not encode those label fields.
Both specify the permitted internal cross-connect combinations within a node.

i.telink is necessarily a link within one specific layer network between per-layer TE nodes, while t.link connects aggregate forwarding nodes in a unified multi-layer topology. The scope and endpoint objects differ materially.
i.tetopo is strictly a separate per-layer TE network; t.topo is the single combined multi-layer domain topology. They therefore denote different topology granularities.

Both denote a node-local endpoint of an internal connection realizing end-to-end connectivity. The service-versus-tunnel parent terminology reflects the surrounding realization model rather than a different endpoint meaning.
